_source: MMG_v19_Client_Manual_Testing_Guideline_FG15-FG20_v1.0.xlsx / Testing Guideline — pulled from the client's Drive on 2026-09-16. FG-18 'Platform Migration & Smoke Readiness' holds 7 cases: TC-SMK-003, -007, -013, -014, -016, -017, -018. All 7 are implemented: 3 pass, 1 fails on a real defect, 3 are blocked by this instance.
_method: TC-SMK-003's 'every menu opens' is a server fact underneath: the action resolves and every view it pins can be BUILT. An 'Invalid view definition' pop-up is precisely a view that would not build, so walking ir.ui.menu.load_menus — the call the web client makes — and calling get_view on each is not an approximation of the case, it is the same question, asked of all 233 menus rather than the handful anyone reaches by hand. What it cannot ask is the browser console; that half stays with TEST-SMOKE-001 and is said out loud in the run log rather than passed over.
_safety: TC-SMK-013 is the one case in this suite that leaves a permanent mark, and it is inherent: confirming an order takes an order number, posting an invoice takes one out of the journal's sequence and writes it into the gallery's books. Deleting the records afterwards does not return the numbers. The workbook asks for exactly these four documents to be created, so there is no version of this case that does not spend them. Everything else is marked, swept and archived only where a posted document pins it — 0 live rows left after the run.

_findings.BC-FG16-001 [RESOLVED] (also fails here): FIXED 2026-09-16. 'Inventory > Operations' was active but gated on base.group_no_one, so the whole branch - Transfers, Deliveries, Receipts, Adjustments including Physical Inventory, and Scrap - reached nobody without Technical Features. The gate was in the DATABASE, not the code: Odoo 19 declares the menu with no groups attribute (addons/stock/views/stock_menu_views.xml:7) and so does Odoo 15 (checked in mmg_15/addons), and nothing in mmg_19-custom touches it - somebody set it by hand on the v15 production database and the restore carried it forward. Removed via the ORM, not SQL, because _visible_menu_ids/load_menus are ormcached and a raw UPDATE leaves the running workers serving the old tree. Menus served went from 233 to 243 and all three cases that failed on it - TC-STU-006, TC-SMK-003, TC-UIX-011 - now pass. Made reproducible in mmg_19-custom/tools/staging19_cleanup.sh step 4g as a third direction, WANT_UNGATED, beside WANT_ON/WANT_OFF, with step 6 verifying it (expect 0 rows), so a fresh staging rebuild reapplies it. NOT swept: the six other menus this database gates the same way - Languages, Database Structure, CRM Tags, Lost Reasons and two Configuration > Products menus - are clutter-hiding and look deliberate, so they are deliberately left alone. ORIGINAL FINDING: TC-SMK-003 step 4 names 'Inventory > Operations > Transfers > Deliveries / Receipts / Internal' and '> Adjustments > Physical Inventory' among the menus a tester must open. All four are ACTIVE and served to nobody: the branch is gated on base.group_no_one on this database, while stock Odoo 19 ships it ungated (addons/stock/views/stock_menu_views.xml:7-10) and nothing in mmg_19-custom touches it. These are the gallery's daily screens. Same defect TC-STU-006 fails on; this case failing on it too is correct, not duplication.
_findings.OBS-FG18-001 [RESOLVED]: CLOSED 2026-09-16 as a documented deliberate removal, not a defect. 'E-commerce Connectors > Products > Product Variants' is archived on purpose: mmg_19-custom/tools/staging19_cleanup.sh step 4g re-archives 'multichannel_product.menu_omniborder_product_variants' on every staging rebuild and cites NOVOBI-514 - MMG hides every Product Variants menu under the connector, and the v15 enforcer (mmg_multichannel_shopify) is FG-10b and not ported. That script IS the removal list TC-SMK-003 step 7 asks for. Measured support: 69,539 templates against 69,539 variants and only 6 templates with more than one variant, so the variant list shows nothing the product list does not; and 'Sales > Products > Product Variants' IS served, so variants themselves are switched on. Encoded as DELIBERATELY_REMOVED + removal_allowed() in tests/fg15/common.py and tests/fg18/common.py. The allowance is deliberately narrow: it is honoured ONLY while the menu is genuinely archived, so a menu that is active and merely unreachable - broken action, missing group - still fails the case and cannot borrow this permission; and every allowance is still logged with its citation and still reported as an observation, so nothing vanishes from the report. ORIGINAL FINDING: 'E-commerce Connectors > Products > Product Variants' is named by TC-SMK-003 step 4 and is ARCHIVED (active=False), as are the Inventory and Purchase entry points to the same screen. 'Sales > Products > Product Variants' IS served, so variants themselves are switched on — it is the other three entry points that are off. Archiving is how Odoo switches a feature's menus off, so this may well be one of the deliberate removals step 7 allows for; only Novobi's removal list can say. Reported separately from the gated menus above because the two want different answers.
_findings.ENV-FG18-001: ENVIRONMENT, not a product defect, and it was silently corrupting results. The Odoo 19 test instance was RESTARTING ITSELF every ~3.5 minutes - 10 reloads in 30 minutes, for at least an hour, with nobody asking for it. Measured from the container log: reloads at 12:11:43, 12:15:06, 12:18:28, 12:21:52, 12:25:16, 12:28:40, 12:33:04, 12:36:30, 12:40:06, 12:43:51. Cause: limit_time_real defaults to 120 and measures the WALL TIME OF THE THREAD, not time spent serving a request. The stacktrace Odoo dumps before each reload names the offender - http/server.py:408 handle_one_request -> socket.py:720 readinto, with (db:n/a) (uid:n/a) (url:n/a). All three are n/a because that thread had never received a request: it was an IDLE HTTP keep-alive socket (a browser tab left open on the instance, a Playwright page between steps) waiting for the next request line. With workers = 0 there is no worker to recycle, so ThreadedServer's only remedy is to reload the whole server, killing every in-flight request. WHAT IT COST: TEST-SMOKE-001 failed as 'Login succeeded: expected True, got False', which reads exactly like a wrong password and is not one - the POST /web/login landed 6 seconds before a reload and the browser was left on /web/login with a blank page. The credentials were correct throughout (RPC login returns uid 78 with the same admin/admin the UI test types, and 44 RPC tests authenticate with it). It is also the likeliest cause of the 'Connection refused' that killed the FG-20 run, which was recorded against TC-PERF-004's bulk write. FIXED 2026-09-16 by setting limit_time_real = 0 in docker/config/odoo19.conf and restarting mmg-odoo19. On a threaded QA instance the watchdog protects nothing - it cannot kill one thread, only the server - while any kept-alive socket trips it. This must NOT be copied to production, where workers > 0 makes it recycle a single worker and do a real job. After the fix: no watchdog trip, POST /web/login returns 303, 'Login successful for login:admin', and TEST-SMOKE-001 PASSES in 108.6s - the remaining time being the cold web.assets_backend build, which is why NAV_TIMEOUT_MS is 180000 in config/local.yaml. NOTE FOR WHOEVER REBUILDS THIS STACK: docker/ is not under version control, so this config change has no history behind it.
_findings.OBS-FG18-002: A 'Magento Images' menu record still exists (Sales > Configuration > Products) but is served to nobody, so no tester will meet it — which is why TC-SMK-003's step 6 assertion is made against the SERVED tree rather than every row. It is the screen for the Studio model x_magento_img, which product.template.x_img_ids and product.product.x_img_ids still point at, and which this same workbook's 'Automated & Novobi Tests' sheet lists as TC-STU-007 'migrate or retire — Decision, not a test'. Not a defect to raise here; evidence for that decision.
_findings.OBS-FG18-003: Invoice and payment numbering is per JOURNAL, not global. This database holds both SHOP/2026/09/0012 and SQ/2026/1779 — two journals' sequences that say nothing about each other. An earlier draft of TC-SMK-013 compared the new payment against the globally-newest one and failed on a pattern mismatch that was not a defect. Step 4 of the workbook says it plainly: 'the highest existing number FOR THE CUSTOMER INVOICE JOURNAL'. The test now reads its baseline per journal, after the document lands.

TC-SMK-003.reason: PASSES as of 2026-09-16. It used to FAIL on BC-FG16-001 plus OBS-FG18-001 — five menus the workbook named by hand were not served. Four of them (the Inventory > Operations branch) are now served, the group_no_one gate having been removed; the fifth, E-commerce Product Variants, is archived ON PURPOSE (NOVOBI-514) and is now an evidenced allowance under step 7's own wording rather than a failure. Everything else passes: every one of the served menus (233 before the ungating, 243 after) resolves its action and builds every list, form and search view it pins, with zero breakages; no Magento menu is visible anywhere. The two causes of the five absences (group-gated vs archived) are separated in the log because they want different answers from Novobi. Residual manual: the browser console, and ticking against the old system's menu list.

TC-SMK-007.reason: PASSES. All thirteen bulk entries are bound to the lists the workbook names them on, and 'Product Certificate' is bound as a REPORT rather than an action — which is exactly what puts it under Print and not under Actions, as the Expected Result requires. The workbook's mapping of restricted entry to controlling right is recorded for the tester. Steps 4-6 (signing in as an ordinary gallery user) are residual manual: which entries a given login is served depends on the rights that login carries, and the workbook asks for one the gallery nominates.

TC-SMK-013.reason: PASSES. A real order, invoice, payment and delivery are created and each number checked three ways against the highest existing one OF ITS OWN JOURNAL: higher, not a duplicate, and the same pattern — the 'restarts at 00001' failure the workbook names. Baselines are read by id, not by name: SO999 sorts above SO1000 alphabetically and would pick the wrong baseline.

TC-SMK-014.reason: BLOCKED, with the measurement that proves it. The instance was restored from `medicinemangallery-staging-19-..._test_nofs.zip` — nofs meaning NO FILESTORE — so the attachment rows came across and the files did not; a sample of the smallest stored files is read back and the shortfall reported. A FAIL here would put a product defect in the client's record for something the restore did on purpose. Needs: a restore that includes the filestore, plus Novobi's list of the 15 named files.

TC-SMK-016.reason: BLOCKED and not automatable in principle. The case turns on three users signing in with their OLD passwords and one passing 2FA with a code from the EXISTING authenticator. A password this platform could supply would be one it had set, which tests nothing about whether the old one survived; a TOTP code needs the phone. The login and 2FA counts are reported so the tester knows what they are working with.

TC-SMK-017.reason: BLOCKED. Steps 1-5 press 'Test Connection', 'Test & Confirm' and 'Fetch Now' against real mail servers, and this database has none: the restore deleted every outgoing and incoming server so a production copy cannot email the gallery's customers. That is the right state for a test instance and the reason the case cannot run on it. What CAN be checked here is checked and passes: no Magento email template survives, and an order-cancellation template is present.

TC-SMK-018.reason: PASSES. Every field label on the six screens the workbook walks is read for an internal-looking name — x_ prefix, lower_case_with_underscores, '[missing]', or blank — and none offends. The gallery's eight product labels and the three contact phone labels are checked by name and the right way round, and there is no 'Phone One', whose absence the workbook says is correct. Residual manual: the 'Assign Customer Taxes' dialog's button wording, and drop-down VALUES, which a field-label sweep cannot see.
